prompt.en: Who suggested the term Dominion of Canada in 1864?
prompt.fr: Qui a proposé l'expression « Dominion du Canada » en 1864?

options.en: Sir Leonard Tilley, a Father of Confederation from New Brunswick.
options.fr: Sir Leonard Tilley, un Père de la Confédération du Nouveau-Brunswick.

explanation.en: The word came from Sir Leonard Tilley in 1864. He sat as an elected member for New Brunswick and was one of the Fathers of Confederation, and he took the idea from a psalm about rule stretching from one sea to another.
explanation.fr: Le mot vient de sir Leonard Tilley, en 1864. Il siégeait comme élu du Nouveau-Brunswick et comptait parmi les Pères de la Confédération; il a tiré l'idée d'un psaume évoquant un règne allant d'une mer à l'autre.

source.quote: Sir Leonard Tilley, an elected official and Father of Confederation from New Brunswick, suggested the term Dominion of Canada in 1864.

verification.evidence: Sir Leonard Tilley, an elected official and Father of Confederation from New Brunswick, suggested the term Dominion of Canada in 1864. He was inspired by Psalm 72 in the Bible which refers to “dominion from sea to sea and from the river to the ends of the earth.”
